title: Remove Token Field from account show and account list Output
description: Remove the Token property from AccountShowView entirely. It currently appears as '***' in 'account show' output and serves no informational purpose — it creates a false impression of a token exposure surface. Confirm AccountListView has no token field. Update all output examples in tests and documentation.
prerequisiteState: Stories 1–22 complete. AccountShowView has a Token property with value '***' that appears in 'account show' output. AccountListView has no token field.
goal: After this story: 'account show' and 'account list' output contains no token or credential fields whatsoever.
scope: Modify src/ZapiCli.Core/Accounts/AccountShowView.cs — delete the Token property (public string Token { get; init; } = "***";) entirely from the record.
Modify src/ZapiCli.Core/Accounts/AccountService.cs — in ShowAccountAsync, remove Token = "***" from the AccountShowView initializer. The returned object must have no token field.
Verify src/ZapiCli.Core/Accounts/AccountListView.cs has no Token property — read the file and confirm. No code change needed if absent.
Update any unit tests that assert on a Token field or '***' in the output for account show — remove those assertions.
Update docs/HELP.md — in the 'account show' Example output section, remove the 'access_token: "***"' line from the JSON example. In any 'account list' example, confirm no token field appears.
Confirm no other test or command references the Token field on AccountShowView or AccountListView after removal (grep for '.Token' and 'Token =' in tests/).
acceptanceCriteria: AccountListView has no Token property (confirmed, no change needed)
'account show' command output contains no 'token' or 'access_token' JSON keys
docs/HELP.md account show example output has no token field
contextForAgent: This is a small, isolated change. The ADR-0008 output contract explicitly states that credentials are never emitted to stdout. The '***' token was a defensive placeholder from an earlier design — it is safe to remove entirely. No migration or backward compatibility concern: this is a developer CLI and the output contract is not externally versioned.
